# National Ignition Facility Experiment Achieved Fusion Ignition

A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory experiment at the National Ignition Facility achieved fusion ignition on December 5, 2022. The U.S. Department of Energy announced the result on December 13.

The experiment delivered 2.05 megajoules of energy to its target and generated 3.15 megajoules of fusion energy. That comparison applies at the target level: it is not a measure of net electricity delivered to the grid, and it does not account for facility-wide electricity use.

The DOE described the achievement as progress toward inertial fusion energy. Many scientific and technological developments are still needed before practical energy production.
